# RETRO: PR #12558 (team 1)

## What worked
- Cross-examination was decisive: each reviewer found distinct issues (Opus: firmware-key/state semantics, restart, test inertness, packaging; Sol: no-input exits, pointer during screensaver). Neutral follow-ups produced independent confirmation of every public claim with no contradictions.
- Fetching the kernel driver (Opus) and ttfx source (Opus follow-up) turned hypotheses into concrete, citable mechanisms.
- Sol completed quickly (7.2 min) and source-only; Opus used review.py for stub scenarios and a mutation check.

## Process deviations (coordinator)
1. Team registry dump (`head -c 2500`) printed about 70 lines, over the 60-line aggregate bound.
2. Seven parallel 50-line diff reads in one response (about 350 lines) exceeded the aggregate bound.
3. Opus follow-up read as three parallel chunks (143 lines) in one response, same violation. Lesson: parallel Read calls count toward the bound; read sequentially.
4. First clone attempt failed (`git clone` does not copy custom `refs/review/*`); preserved in source/failed-attempt-1 with receipts.
5. `git merge-tree --name-only` (object-writing in default mode) was run against the coordinator's own intake repo `source/repo`; an accompanying echo falsely stated it was not run. Loose objects only; reviewers were directed not to use that repo; nothing pruned. Lesson: never pair a command with a message asserting it did not run; use `git diff --stat` for drift checks.
Impact on evidence: none of these touched reviewer checkouts or reviewer evidence; technical claims rest on reviewer reports and follow-ups.

## Friction / improvements
- The `omarchy-reviewer` agent definition does not carry the first-call rules (filename-only listings, 60-line bound). The mandated one-line dispatch means those rules first reach the reviewer inside the brief, which is itself over 50 lines. Suggest adding the first-call rules to the agent definition's system prompt.
- Node.js is not available inside review.py, so `idle-test.sh` JS assertions could not run. Pre-staging node as a fixture tool would help shell-model PRs.
- review.py snapshots fail on the absolute symlink `config/omarchy/plugins/omacom.elsewhen`; reviewers had to scope snapshots.

## Carry forward
- For brightness/LED PRs, check how hardware keys are routed (firmware vs userspace) early.
- For idle-service PRs, distinguish input-only vs inhibitor-obeying idle notifications in Hyprland.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the idle timeout is opt-in and inert when `idle.keyboardBacklight` is absent or `0`. The separate `IdleMonitor` uses input-only idle notification, so Stay Awake and idle inhibitors do not keep the LED lit, as documented. The single-slot command queue is sound: Quickshell 0.3.1 clears `running` before `onExited`, so the pending command starts. The stacked #12553 commits also fix a base bug: dismissing the screensaver no longer reverts a level chosen with the brightness keys to an older brightnessctl snapshot, and a second `off` (idle, then lock) no longer saves `0`.

Four behaviour issues follow. The first comes from the stacked #12553 commits (`9a46700e`, `7ca8b3d9`), and this PR's timeout makes it run on every idle cycle. The other three are in `104b880d`.

### A backlight turned off outside the script comes back on

`off` now skips `brightnessctl -s` when the LED is already `0`, and `restore` prefers the `XDG_STATE_HOME` state file, falling back to an earlier brightnessctl save (`bin/omarchy-brightness-keyboard` lines 57-71). A level changed outside the script is therefore undone. On ThinkPads this is the normal path: `thinkpad_acpi` handles Fn+Space (`TP_HKEY_EV_KBD_LIGHT`) in firmware and suppresses the key event by default, so Omarchy's `cycle` binding never runs.

```text
Sequence (idle.keyboardBacklight set)      base (60663faf)   head (104b880d)
LED on (2), idle -> off, input -> restore        2                 2
Fn+Space turns LED off in firmware               0                 0
idle -> off                                  saves 0           no save
input -> restore                                 0                 2  <- relit
```

Reproduced with a brightnessctl stub modelled on brightnessctl 0.5.1 save/restore order; not reproduced on hardware.

**Impact:** with the timeout enabled, a user who switches the keyboard light off with a firmware-handled key gets it switched back on after the next idle period. The same happens across a lock and unlock without the timeout.

**Suggested change:** let `off` tell "this script blanked a lit LED" from "the LED was already 0", for example with a runtime marker written only when `off` blanks a nonzero level, and save `0` when no marker exists. That keeps the double-blank fix and respects a deliberate `0`.

### The keyboard relights while the user is still away

When the main idle cycle ends without input, `cancelIdleCycle` runs `omarchy-system-wake`, which calls `omarchy-brightness-keyboard restore` (`shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml` lines 117-128). The keyboard monitor saw no input, so `isIdle` stays true and no second `off` follows.

```text
keyboard monitor idle -> off
screensaver closes without input (focus taken by a new or activating window)
  -> cancelIdleCycle -> omarchy-system-wake -> keyboard restore   (LED on)
keyboard monitor: still idle, no transition -> LED stays on
```

Omarchy's defaults (`focus_on_activate = true`, `on_focus_under_fullscreen = 1`) let an activating or newly mapped window take focus from the screensaver, which then exits. The LED stays lit until the next lock screen blanks it (about lock timeout + 5 s with defaults), or for the whole absence if that window holds an idle inhibitor. Turning Stay Awake on during an idle cycle without local input (SSH, script, unattended `omarchy update -y`) has the same effect with no lock to follow. Not a regression against base, where the LED stays lit through the screensaver anyway, but the "dark while idle" behaviour lapses on these paths. Source-derived.

**Impact:** the timeout can leave the keyboard lit for minutes, or the rest of an absence, while no one is at the machine.

**Suggested change:** after the wake in `cancelIdleCycle`, enqueue `omarchy-brightness-keyboard --no-osd off` again when `keyboardBacklightTimeoutEnabled && keyboardBacklightMonitor.isIdle`. The input-only monitor's `isIdle` is not reset by focus or inhibitor changes, so it is a reliable "no input since" signal.

### Pointer movement does not restore the keyboard during the screensaver

After the keyboard `off`, pointer motion sends `resumed` to the keyboard monitor, but `handleKeyboardBacklightIdleChanged` returns at `if (root.idledThisCycle) return` (`Service.qml` lines 206-208), and that transition is consumed. `bin/omarchy-screensaver` exits only on a tty byte, focus loss or a signal, and ttfx enables no mouse reporting, so pointer motion does not dismiss the screensaver either. The keyboard stays dark until a key press or the lock screen. The new manual text says the light returns "when you type or move the pointer" (`manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md` line 81). Source-derived; not observed in a live session.

**Impact:** the documented pointer restore does not happen while the screensaver is showing.

**Suggested change:** either reword the manual (for example, "while the screensaver is showing, press a key"), or reconsider the `idledThisCycle` skip. In Hyprland 0.56.2 source, the pseudo-activity at screensaver start comes from focus-driven inhibitor rechecks, which reach only inhibitor-obeying notifications, so the input-only keyboard monitor does not appear to see it. That reading is untested and needs a live check before removing the guard.

### A shell restart during an idle-dark period leaves the keyboard dark

A new `IdleMonitor` starts with `isIdle` false, and Hyprland sends `resumed` only to a notification that has already sent `idled`. If the shell restarts while the LED is dark from the timeout (for example, `omarchy update` restarts the shell) and the user returns before `keyboardBacklight` seconds pass, no transition fires. `Component.onCompleted` does not restore (`Service.qml` lines 389-393). Source-derived; not run.

**Impact:** the keyboard stays dark despite activity until a later idle-then-activity cycle.

**Suggested change:** issue one `restore` from `Component.onCompleted` when the timeout is enabled. The login unit already restores at session start, so a duplicate restore is harmless.

**Disable path:** `onKeyboardBacklightTimeoutEnabledChanged` restores whenever an armed timeout is disabled, whether or not the LED is dark (`Service.qml` lines 213-217). This includes a transient default fallback while `shell.json` is briefly invalid. The PR description says it restores only when dark. Suggested change: gate it on an "`off` issued and not yet restored" flag, or adjust the description.

**Documentation:** the new JSON example in `manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md` (lines 83-89) omits `"version": 1`. Copied as a complete `shell.json`, the shell rejects it and uses defaults with only a console warning, so the timeout silently stays off. Suggested change: include `"version": 1`, or show it as a key to add inside the existing `idle` block.

**Packaging:** omarchy-pkgs master does not yet install `omarchy-keyboard-backlight.service`; omarchy-pkgs#538 adds it and is linked from #12553. Fresh installs mark all shipped migrations complete, and first-run ignores a failed `enable`, so installs built before #538 ships would never get the unit enabled. `test/shell.d/config-test.sh` also fails its PKGBUILD check until then. Shipping both in the same release avoids the gap.

**Optional test improvement:** the bare `! grep -F ...` lines in `test/shell.d/keyboard-backlight-test.sh` (lines 21-22) cannot fail, because `set -e` ignores `!`-negated commands. A mutation adding both forbidden strings to the script still passed the test; rewriting them as `if grep -F ...; then fail ...; fi` made it fail.

In an isolated sandbox: `keyboard-backlight-test.sh` passed 9/9, per-script `bash -n`, a mutation check of that test, the migration under `bash -euo pipefail` against a stubbed `systemctl`, and brightness-script sequences against a brightnessctl stub on head and base.
